title: Watch: Ceddanne Rafaela hits home runs in back-to-back at-bats
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Ceddanne Rafaela of the Boston Red Sox hit two home runs in consecutive at-bats against the Los Angeles Dodgers.
Rafaela's home runs were against Dodgers pitcher Yoshinobu Yamamoto, tying the game at two with a 402-foot shot.
Rafaela's performance improved his season total to 14 homers, continuing his strong hitting in Dodger Stadium.

title: Red Sox reportedly attempted to acquire shortstop Elly De La Cruz, turned down by Reds
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Red Sox attempted to trade for Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz but couldn't agree on deal terms.
Boston's offer to Cincinnati for De La Cruz was primarily based on prospects, according to MassLive's Sean McAdam.
The Red Sox are seeking middle infield upgrades due to injuries, with Trevor Story expected to return soon.

title: Drake Maye says his shoulder ‘feels great’ as Patriots training camp continues
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Drake Maye reports his shoulder is fully recovered as the New England Patriots continue training camp in Foxborough.
Patriots have bolstered their offense, adding receiver A.J. Brown to complement Drake Maye's passing attack.
A.J. Brown adjusts to the Patriots' playbook quickly, becoming an integral part of the wide receiver corps.

title: If July’s stretch of dominance wasn’t enough, the Red Sox’ win Friday proved they’re plenty capable of a postseason run
author: Colin McCarthy
bullets: Boston Red Sox defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 5-4, continuing their dominant winning streak in July.
Ceddanne Rafaela's pivotal plays turned a 4-3 deficit into a win, highlighting the team's resilience.
Despite missing key players, the Red Sox showcased strong depth and potential for a postseason run.

title: Red Sox fend off Dodgers, 9-4, in grindy series opener
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: The Boston Red Sox defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 9-4 in the series opener at Dodger Stadium.
Ceddanne Rafaela hit a crucial two-run home run in the seventh inning, giving Boston a 5-4 lead.
Reliever Brayan Bello pitched four scoreless innings, helping maintain the lead and secure the win.

title: Gabe Jacas makes his Patriots debut and other takeaways from Day 7 of training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Gabe Jacas, a Patriots' 2026 second-round pick, made a limited practice debut after recovering from a knee procedure.
Patriots' practice on Saturday featured an unscripted format, with Drake Maye leading an offense-defense tug-of-war.
Undrafted free agent Tanner Arkin is gaining attention for his blocking skills, earning first-team reps in Patriots camp.

title: Mass. to be 4th state to roll out EBT chip cards to curb fraud
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Massachusetts will roll out chip-enabled EBT cards statewide to combat fraud, becoming the fourth state to adopt this technology.
Nearly 1 million residents use SNAP benefits at 5,500 retailers, with the state issuing $2.6 billion annually.
New cards will reduce theft risk from devices like skimmers and include features like app-based card lock/unlock capabilities.

title: Boston is now offering ‘pet certificates’ for couples who wed at City Hall
author: Morgan Rousseau
bullets: Boston City Hall now offers pet certificates for couples marrying there, allowing pets to be officially recognized in ceremonies.
Mayor Michelle Wu announced that the certificates celebrate pets' roles in family life, featuring the City of Boston's playful department names.
The first pet certificate was awarded to Bono the golden retriever during a City Hall wedding officiated by Boston Registrar Paul Chong.

title: Kevin Nealon discusses Conan, Dunkin’, SNL and more ahead of local shows
author: Lauren Daley
bullets: Kevin Nealon announced comedy shows in Boston and Portsmouth, New Hampshire, this week.
Nealon uses Twitter to showcase comedic bits, promoting his special 'Loose in the Crotch' on YouTube.
He discusses his career, from Dunkin' in Connecticut to SNL and movies with Adam Sandler.

title: Red Sox’ Willson Contreras leaves game after scary HBP vs. Dodgers
author: Kaley Brown
bullets: Willson Contreras was hit by a 95 MPH fastball from Dodgers pitcher Will Klein in the third inning.
Contreras stayed in the game to take his base but was removed later for precautionary reasons by the Red Sox.
Red Sox interim manager Chad Tracy stated Contreras is doing well but his return depends on Saturday's health evaluation.
